utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We understand, Mr. Saxon, that there are all sorts of changes necessary because of changes in the health situation and other problems concerning witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is correct Your Honour. The witness who was testifying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Don't bother. Putting it all on the record. We understand there are problems and they will resolve in time and we are moving on temporarily to a fresh witness with a view to returning to finish the unfinished witness. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. And Ms. Regue will lead the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, unfortunately, with the movement to and fro and the taking the oaths we never get this in the right order. You're about to announce your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution would like to call Farush Memedi, witness M-57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Memedi.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, do you recall providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You recall providing a statement, another statement, a brief one, to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2005?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with a lady from the registry of this Tribunal to certify, meaning put a stamp on both your statements also in 2005?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Before coming here, Mr. Memedi, did you have the opportunity to read both the statements in your native language?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that its content is correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to tender both the statements pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P266, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The witness, Farush Memedi is a Ljuboten resident of Albanian ethnicity. Between 10 to 12 August 2001 Macedonian forces attacked Ljuboten with gun-fire and shelling, causing the death of one civilian Tari Murati and the wounding of an another Femi Latifi. On Sunday, 12 August, the witness heard intensive shooting and shelling since 8.00 a.m. in the morning. Around noon of the same day a large number of Ljuboten residents, including the witness and his family, decided to leave the village and arrived at Buzalak check-point. Here the police ordered the men to be separated from the women. The men, including the witness, were ordered to lie down and were beaten by the police. They were then transported by police by a police van to Cair or Butel police station, where they were beaten again. They were later taken to Kisela Voda or Prolece police station where they were beaten again. In the evening of 12 August, the police tied the witness's hand on his back with tape. He could not believe that something was being done to his fingers. Afterward he was submitted to the paraffin test and was forced to sign a document, the contents which were unknown to him. After approximately 24 hours, the witness and other detainees were taken to Skopje Hospital where he saw other detainees being mistreated. After approximately one day, the witness was taken to Skopje Court where he appeared before a judge. The witness was then transported to Sutka prison where he remained for about four months. Your Honours, we have some binders for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if we could please -- thanks. Could we please have 65 ter 199.21. It's the photo depicted in tab 3 of your binder and also it's the photo on page 15 of the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, what do you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: We can see here the police check-point. Here was the police check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what is the name of this police check-point?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: They call it Buzalak, but someone calls it also Kodra e Zajmit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where it's located, this check-point?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This check-point was located exactly at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But if we took as a reference Ljuboten, could you approximately say how far is it, how many kilometres from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes. It's approximately four to five kilometres from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. In paragraph 10 to 12 of your statement you explain that on Sunday, the 12th of August, of 2001, you and your family left Ljuboten and arrived at the Buzalak check-point. What happened when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: The police was there at the check-point. They stopped us. They separated men from women. They forced us to lay down and they started to mistreat us, to beat us, to hit us with guns. Children started to scream, and they boarded us on a van and sent us to a station, to a police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If I could have, please, the usher's assistance in helping the witness with a pen. Mr. Memedi, could you please take the pen that the usher is going to give to you. And first of all, could you mark with a cross where the check-point is from -- in the photo?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: The check-point was located here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you write number one next to the cross, please.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: On the check-point?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw a circle in the area where the men were forced to lying down and then write number 2.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw a circle in the area where the women were ordered to go and write number 3.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Memedi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit P267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to call ERN N004-4980. It's the photo depicted in the court binder, page 18, photo A. For Your Honours, it's the first tab.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, what do you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This photo represents the police station Butel.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you taken this police station on Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P268, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to call ERN N004-4998. It is the photo depicted in the court binder, page 19, photo B. Also tab 2 for Your Honours. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, what do you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This is a cell at the Butel police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When you were taken to Butel, were you placed in a cell which looked like this one?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P269, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'd like to call Exhibit P51, page 96. It's the last tab in Your Honour's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, are you able to see the Macedonian version on the right side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you don't see it properly, please let us know, because we have a hard copy for you.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Memedi, if you look at the upper left corner of this document, in the first line do you see Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And then three lines below, 13 August 2001, Skopje. Do you see that, Mr. Memedi?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Then if we move to the centre of this document, do you see the title, Official Note, and the numbers 536?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And then below, the title official interview conducted with persons who were apprehended from the village of Ljuboten. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm going read to you the first lines of the first paragraph: "On 12 August 2001 at the premises of OVR Kisela Voda, I had interviews with nine persons who were taken from the village of Ljuboten by the associated security forces of the Republic of Macedonia." And then in these first paragraphs we see a list of names. Do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you the second and the third paragraph: "As a result of the interviews conducted with the above-mentioned persons, it was acknowledged that all of them, these nine persons, were present in the village in time when combat activities were carried out by the security forces in the village of Ljuboten. They stated the following in regard of the events that occurred there. "Shooting could you heard at each side of the village. Actually, fight was led between the police of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist gangs. The above-mentioned persons stated they noticed many terrorists engaged in fights, having weapons but about themselves they stated that they did not take part in the fights but they wanted to flee from the village. Some of them wanted to surrender to the police because they did not take part in the fights." Mr. Memedi, when you were in Kisela Voda also known as Prolece, were you ever interviewed by someone from the police?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you state, did you say to someone what it says in this document?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Also from your knowledge, what it's written in here is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think the question of my colleague should be rephrased to ask him what he personally knows. The question leave its open what he is being asked, whether he's going to ask whether other people knew it, whether anyone else knew it. I think it should be specified and ask him what his position is. I don't think he can give evidence for anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said from his knowledge if he knew whether these facts were correct. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I know. His knowledge, though, could be understood, as Mr. Mettraux suggests, what he has heard from others. Clearly you didn't intend that, but it could be understood that way. I think as is suggested we should for the moment, at least, concentrate on what this witness knows about what happened to him and his interview. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, did you see from your own eyes what it says in this document?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We could take out this document from the screen, Your Honours. I have no further questions concerning this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, when you were in prison in Sutka, were you ever interviewed by someone from the police or the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And I should say and my question was if you were interviewed about what happened to you about what happened in Ljuboten, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sure. If when you were in Sutka prison and afterwards someone from the police or from the Ministry of Interior came to ask you about what had happened to you or what had happened in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, you testified that in Buzalak check-point you were taken and beaten by police. You also mentioned that you were taken to Butel by police officers. Were you beaten in Butel?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 15/16 you also mention that afterwards you were taken to Kisela Vode, Prolece police station. Were you beaten there?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, they beat us there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt again, but all of that evidence is in evidence. We have a statement that has been tendered. The whole point of Rule 92 bis is precisely to accelerate matters and to allow the evidence in chief to put through with a statement. We're going through the same grounds, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If Your Honour wish, I can just say everything that is in the statement and then phrase my final question. But in fairness to my learned colleague, I wanted just to lay the ground before I asked witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you are simply wanting the evidence of the witness to be what is in the statement, as it's 92 bis, you really need to ask no more questions about it. If there's something you want to be amplified or made more clear or some additional matter, certainly ask questions. But there's no point in us having the statement and then having the oral evidence as well, if it's the same. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will move to the question then.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, in all the locations that you mentioned in your statement, you explained that you saw police officers. How were the uniforms of the police?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: They had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you able to see any patch in the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes. They had an insignia, police insignia, on their arm, and it was insignia of the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Regue. Mr. Mettraux, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Memedi. My name is Guenael Mettraux and together with my colleague Edina Residovic I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski. Could the witness please be shown what is now Exhibit P267. Sir, you were just shown a picture, a picture will appear on your screen which has been shown to you by my colleague a moment ago. Do you have that picture in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You were asked by my colleague to state the name of this location and at page 4, line 8 of the transcript, you said that this place was known as Kodra e Zajmit or as Buzalak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: It is called Buzalak, but some people refer to it as Kodra e Zajmit. I don't know how to explain it to you, but this place has two names.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, sir, that Kodra e Zajmit in Macedonian is known as Zamski Ridge and not at Buzalak?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, in Macedonian it is called Zamski Rid. That's correct. It's called Zamski Rid in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And isn't that correct that Buzalak and Kodra e Zajmit are, in fact, two different locations and that Kodra e Zajmit is further down three or four kilometres towards Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I wouldn't say three or four kilometres towards Skopje. It's much closer. I know this place very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree, sir, that in fact Kodra e Zajmit and Buzalak are not one and the same place. They are distant from each other. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This is my native place, and you cannot know it better than myself. Kodra e Zajmit, it's a little bit further down. Buzalak, it's a little bit more up. So this location that we see on the photograph is neither on Buzalak or Kodra e Zajmit. It's between these two locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you're quite right. It's your location and not mine. So if someone from the location just like you were to say that they are two different places separate from between three on four kilometres, would that person be correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I'm telling you the truth. This location is not on Buzalak or Kodra e Zajmit. That's why I mentioned both Buzalak and Kodra e Zajmit, because this particular location is neither on Buzalak or Kodra e Zajmit. It's between the two locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So we can agree, sir, that this position here is not Kodra e Zajmit; is that correct? Kodra e Zajmit is further south towards Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes. Buzalak is a little bit more up.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like you turn now to a different document that was also shown to you by my learned colleague of the Prosecution, and, Your Honour, it's been shown to you under P51, page 96. We have a different reference. It's the same document, Your Honour, and it's also been admitted as P53 with an ERN ET-N001-983901, and I'm going to use this one, with the Court's permission. It's also been admitted. And the Macedonian is N001-9827-13. Sir, the document that will appear on your screen is the Official Note which was shown a moment ago by my colleague to you. Do you have the Macedonian in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, but one can hardly read from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, Your Honour, what I will do, I will use the version of the Prosecution with a risk of some slight translation issues, if that's feasible. If the copy -- Can you see it now, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: It's a little bit better.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, have you seen that document before today?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Was it shown to you during the week here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can draw your attention to the first paragraph of that document which starts with the word "On 12/08/2001." Can you see that? That is paragraph the under the subject heading, sir. It says, "On 12 August 2001 in the premise of" and goes on to say ... You see, sir, that your name is mentioned at the end of this paragraph. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also see that in the previous sentence it says this: "They were identified and later on through interviews and examination with these same persons, it was confirmed that these men are as follows." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you indicated to my colleague that it is your evidence that you were not interviewed by the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you examined by the police?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we go to the last paragraph, sir, of this document, there's a list of names. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the first name on the list is yours, Memedi Farush, farther --

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Born 27 March 1965, village of Ljuboten. Are those -- that data is correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a list of name of other individuals. Can you see those?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those people, sir, they were also present at Kisola Voda or Prolece police station at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you, sir.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you're not disputing having had contact with police officers during that day at Kisela Voda, sir, are you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I was at the police station but they did not ask me about anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's look at the previous paragraph. It started with the word: "Shots of weapons could be heard coming out from each side of the village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that is consistent with your own observation on the 12th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "Actually combat activity were led between the police of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist gangs. The aforenamed persons stated that they noticed many terrorists fighting and were having fire-arms in their hands." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say, "Nevertheless, themselves, they didn't take part in the fights," they said, said they. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "They wanted to run away from the village and some of them wanted to surrender to police as they did not take part in the fights," sir. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that last part of the statement, sir, is correct, isn't it, that you didn't take part in the fight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... What you wanted also was to flee from the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also wanted to surrender to the police or was it something you were not intent on doing?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I was with my family with my children, and I simply wanted to go towards Skopje, towards the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So in fact, sir, the only part of this document with which you take an issue is the suggestion that there were combat activities between the Macedonian forces and terrorists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, sir, do you mean to say that you did not see any such thing, combat activities between Macedonian forces and terrorists and you say, no, I didn't say that. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: There was no NLA in Ljuboten. The bottom line is that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understand the bottom line, sir. Perhaps I'll ask you this at this stage: Is what you're saying is you are saying you did not say that there were combat activities between the NLA and Macedonian forces to a police officer in the police station Kisela Voda; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Well, what was I supposed to tell them when they didn't ask me anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think that answers my question, sir. But you're not denying, are you, that any of the other eight persons who are mentioned on that document might have said that to the police officer, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, you intervened and stopped Ms. Regue when a question of hers could have been understood as asking beyond this man's knowledge. Now you are the biter bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I plead guilty, Your Honour. I will ask the question differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, have you had an opportunity to discuss this matter with any of the other eight persons mentioned on the document?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't show interest to discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, I think you've mentioned to one of my early question that your bottom line was that the NLA members were not in the village on that day. Do you remember telling me this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I earlier said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, sir, in fact that is only a guess on your part. You're not in a position to say whether they were or were not in the village on that day, are you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I didn't see anything there. When we arrived at the check-point we were stopped by the police and maltreated. This was it. And there was shooting in Ljuboten -- I mean shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, sir, is you are not in a position to say whether they were members of the NLA in the village on the 10, 11 until the 12th around 12.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: There was no NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, could you please answer my question. You were not in a position on the 10th, 11th and until the 12th of August, 2001, to see whether or not there were NLA members in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I was at home. When I went outside I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, sir, let's then go back to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is P266. It's just been tendered by my colleague of the Prosecution. And if we could see the second page of that document. If the registry could focus first on paragraph 3 of that statement, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is the statement which was your statement which was tendered earlier by my colleague and which you have stated to be accurate. If you look at paragraph 3, sir, that's when you start recounting the events of the 10 of August. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the second -- at the second sentence it says: "I remember that at around 8.00 a.m. one morning in August, it might have been a Friday, the shelling and shooting started from the hill in the north above Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry to turn to the next page in the Macedonian. It's the same page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to look at paragraph 4 of your statement. It says this: "I think it was around 10.00 a.m. when the shelling and shooting stopped. I spent the rest of the day home with my family." So in fact, sir, from Friday 8.00 onwards, you spent the entire day with your family at home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to the Saturday now. If you can focus on paragraph 5 of your statement. It starts: "The following day we could hear from time to time some shooting." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you now to look at paragraph 6 of your statement it says this --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to move to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Paragraph 6 says this, sir: "We spent the day and the following night in our house. We could not sleep because we were very afraid and very worried about what would happen to us." So, again, sir, you spent the entire Saturday in your home with your family, day and night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's now turn to the Sunday morning. You will see it starts at paragraph 7 and it goes on to paragraph 10, I believe. It says: "The following morning, that's a Sunday, it must have been Sunday, at around 8.00 a.m. I heard that very intensive shooting and shelling with all kinds of weapons started." Can you see that? It's the first line of paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you go to paragraph 8 you explain that at around 9.00 a.m. or shortly thereafter, you moved from your own house to the basement of the house of Daut Memedi, a cousin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's where you stayed until 12, when you left sir. That's paragraph 10; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. So when I told you earlier that you were not in a position to see what was going on in the village, that was correct, wasn't it? You stayed in your house from the Friday, 8.00 in the morning until the Sunday, 12.00, with a transfer to the house of Daut Memedi on the 12th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were not in a position to assess whether or not there were any NLA members in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Myself, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, but you were not in a position to see any, sir, because you were in your house or in the house of Daut Memedi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I didn't see any NLA there, present.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me ask you another thing then. If the army, the police, the OSCE, the European monitors and the ICRC were all saying that there was NLA presence in the village, you would not say that they were wrong, do you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, you would say that they are all wrong, sir, is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I personally didn't see any NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My question was different. Are you in a position to say whether or not those organisation would be wrong, if they were saying that there was NLA presence in the village?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: There was no NLA in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if all of those organisations or institution were to say that there was an intense armed confrontation between the NLA and Macedonian forces on that day, are you also saying that they would all be wrong, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Well, you can call them and ask them about this and they can tell you about what they have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, have you been told not to mention the presence of the NLA in the village on that day, or on those days?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I didn't see any NLA in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, have you been asked by anyone not to mention the presence of the NLA in the village on 10, 11 and 12 of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. I personally didn't see any NLA presence in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps that may be the translation, but I'm asking you a slightly different question. I'm asking you whether you have been asked by anyone not to mention the presence of the NLA in the village during that weekend.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. Nobody asked me anything. This is what I'm personally telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. We'll move on to evidence which you gave to my colleague about what you say happened to you in the Prolece and Kisola Voda, that's one and the same, police station. Do you remember answering question of my colleague in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question. It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, it wasn't clear. Sir, do you recall answering a number of question from my colleague about what happened to you in the Prolece police station?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked about a statement, whether it was correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also told my colleague that you were mistreated at Prolece police station; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your statement, sir, there's something you've apparently omitted to mention to the Office of the Prosecution, and that's the fact that a number of police officers at Prolece police station tried to protect you from any mistreatment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you omitted to mention to the Office of the Prosecution is that the people who attempted to mistreat you were police reservists. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that people who tried to shield you from the mistreatment was the police commander, the commander of the police station, and the regular police. Isn't that the case, sir, that's what they tried to do, to protect you from the police reservists?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. They were all wearing masks and were ill treating us. They would curse us and we would -- we were just lying down and they were hitting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that we're clear, sir, are you now saying that no one, no member of the police force in Kisola Voda or Prolece police station tried to protect you from any further mistreatment? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So no, this did not happen; that's your evidence. No one tried to protect you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask the registry to bring up 1D185 under the ERN 1D00-2071, that's the English. And the Macedonian is 1D00-2074.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see from the first page, sir, this is the record of interviews taken from Ljuboten residents by the OSCE. Can you see that on the first page?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The source of that document is Mr. Andrew Palmer, senior rule of law officer, OSCE, spill-over monitor mission to Skopje. Can you see that on the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the receiver of that document is Mr. Dan Saxon, trial attorney, OTP. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the date that appears at the bottom of the page which seems to be the date when it was transmitted which is the 25th of October, 2005. You agree?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask the registry to turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, can you see a list of names with case file code and --

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to focus on the number 18, 1-8, of that list, can you see it? It says TB 027, 13.01.02-3 and follows the name Farush Memedi. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I ask the registry to turn to the next page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask you first to focus on the first line of that document. It say this: "Interview on 13 January 2002 in Ljuboten was released due to presidential pardon." Can you see that first line?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there is a number [Previous translation continues] ... which is TB 027-13.01.02/3. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that's the same number that appeared on the previous page next to your name. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This is the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It looks like it is the same, yes, sir. If the -- if you go to the next line it says this: "TBHDU Marie van Baltenar [phoen] in Ljuboten conducted the interview on 13.01.02 with the release from presidential pardon." You can still see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask you now to go to the bottom of that page to look at the last paragraph which starts with the words: "At 0200." It says this: "At 0200 at 13.08.01 one police officer come to the room and I got water, end of beating. At 1500 hours the shift changed. Some reservists wanted to enter and the beating started again. They yelled and screamed. The commander of the police station in civil dressed asked for assistance from the regular police. The 200 -- 200 and -- 200 or 300 or 200 and dash 30 reservists had sticks. The regular police come and got the reservists out. At 0718 hours the beating started again by masked police. I was kicked on my leg and in my chest. I started to cry. The commander exchanged the police. After that, I was not maltreated. At 24 hours I was offered medical service. We left on 14.08.01 for the hospital. On 10.08.01 I was brought to court, accused of terrorism. A public defence lawyer was appointed." Sir, that's what you told the OSCE representative, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I think that the first question will be whether this witness recalls the interview by the OSCE. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It wasn't, Mr. Mettraux, but it will be, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, I do not remember this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting you never met with any representative of the OSCE, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you recall saying this to a person or representative from any particular organisation upon your release?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, is there another Farush Memedi living in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. There is no other -- it is only me, but I don't remember this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if a representative of the OSCE was referring to Farush Memedi and to the fact that she had an interview with Farush Memedi on 13 January 2002 after release from prison, that would be you, sir, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: It could be me, but I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that not be anyone else, there was no -- you've indicated no Farush Memedi from Ljuboten, and none that was detained and released pursuant to a presidential pardon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This is correct. There is a Farush, but there is no Memedi. But I don't remember the statement. I thought that we had given a statement only to The Hague representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall that someone after you were released from prison came to ask you questions, didn't you, and that was in the early days of January -- or in the early days of 2002. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, at this stage we'll seek to tender this document with the caveat obviously that there may be an issue of the weight at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The statement will be marked for identification at the moment. There is nothing to verify that it's been made, it's denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps just a matter of clarification, Your Honour, if I may ask my colleague to state what objection the Prosecution has to the admission of that document which may be relevant to later attempts on our part to use this material.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to know first which is the reasons -- which is the basis why my learned colleague is seeking to tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Neither set of answers -- questions will be answered. If would you continue with your questioning, Mr. Mettraux, the document is marked for identification and not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, from Prolece police station you've indicated that you were taken to the court in Skopje. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Where were you taken first from the police station?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I -- when I became aware, I was at the city hospital. I don't remember how I was taken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not sure I have understood your answer properly, sir. Are you saying that you went first to the hospital and from the hospital to the court?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While you are pausing, Mr. Mettraux, I'll ask the registry officer to indicate the number of the document marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 1D185 will become Exhibit 1D48, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I mention so that it doesn't confuse people later, that due to an interesting characteristic of the search systems, when we are marking a document for identification, the registry officer has to identify it as an exhibit and then adds "marked for identification." If it's not identified as an exhibit, some of the search facilities will not operate with respect to it. But let it be very clear it is not an exhibit. It is merely marked for identification and by the addition of that phrase and designation, it will be clear to all that it is not yet part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to take you to the time when you were taken to the court. Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And to an answer of my learned colleague, you were asked about uniform worn by the police. Can you remember being asked about that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, I think you indicated that the police officers you saw were wearing camouflage uniform and had insignia. You said insignias of the Macedonian police. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, did you mean to indicate that this is also the observation that you made at the court police or was it an observation you only made in relation to other locations?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I saw it at the court and in other police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it the case, sir, that apart from one individual, you were not in a position to see what uniform they were wearing at the court?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My suggestion to you is that, aside from one particular policeman, you were not in a position to observe any of the other uniform worn by police officers present at the court on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Why wasn't I to see them -- in a position to see them? They are there in the hall lined up. They are left here at the corner in the hall. There were police officers present there. We were brought in by other police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are saying now, sir, that you were able to see that they were wearing camouflage uniforms and that they had police patches on their shoulders. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask that the witness be shown P266. It would be the fifth page of the document, paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is again the statement which you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. At paragraph 22 you said the following: "Around midnight or after midnight the police took the four of us to Skopje Court where I could see lots of men, maybe 20 or so, from the Ljuboten village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "I could not recognise any of them because they were all covered" --

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "We were ordered to sit next to them." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then you say: "There was a policeman in camouflage uniform carrying an automatic weapon who was guarding us. Another policeman was walking on the corridor and if one of us would move a bit, he would immediately go on and beat with him something that he had in his hand." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's all you told the Prosecution at the time about what happened to you in the corridor at the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I haven't spoken at the court. I said nothing at the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm -- perhaps you have misunderstood my question or I put to you a poorly phrased question. What I read out to you is the only evidence which you gave to the Prosecution when you were first interviewed on the 30th of 2004 [sic], and I'm talking about what happened to you in the corridor of the Skopje Court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then two days ago, sir, you were interviewed once again by the Prosecution, is that correct, you had a meeting with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during that interview, sir, you said this to the Prosecution. You said that when you were in that corridor you were told to look down and to cover your face with a T-shirt. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: To cover our face with T-shirt. I don't understand the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, two days ago you recall having a meeting with the Prosecution during which you were asked a number of question about what happened to you in the corridor of the Skopje Court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on that occasion you told a representative of the Prosecution that you were told by the policeman to look down and to cover your face with a T-shirt, is that correct, or with a shirt, I'm sorry, with a shirt?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. We didn't have our head covers. We had our head down -- turned down and with eyes turned down entering the corridor and we were not allowed to see. I don't understand the question, what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you were recorded as saying that you were told by the policeman to cover your face with your shirt, that would obviously be a mistake of the person who recorded your statement. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I didn't cover my head with a shirt. At the police station, yes, but not in the court. This is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if you were to be recorded as suggesting that you were told at the court on the corridor of the court to cover your face with your shirt, that would be wrong, is that correct, if you haven't told that to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. Maybe they have made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Right. But you were told, sir, that -- on that same day when you met with the Prosecution, you also told them that you were told to turn around and to face the wall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, to face the wall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you made it clear to the Prosecution when you met with them that you could not see who among those policemens were beating you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you were interviewed once more by the Prosecution very briefly yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And yesterday what you told the Prosecution is that you remembered that all the police officers, all the policemen that you witnessed on that day were wearing camouflage uniforms. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also told the Prosecution yesterday, 13 of June, that the uniforms that you saw had patches with the word "police" on the sleeves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, is that also correct that you -- apart from the one policeman which we've mentioned from your statement, you had never mentioned having seen more than one camouflage uniform at Skopje Court in any of your prior statements?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I have seen police officers in the Skopje Court with camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just focussing on my question, sir, prior to yesterday and aside from the one policeman whom you expressly identified as wearing a camouflage uniform, you never said or you never suggested to the Office of the Prosecution or to anyone else that you had seen camouflage uniform being worn at Skopje Court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Maybe they didn't ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in none of your earlier statements or meetings with the Prosecution did you ever mention having seen patches on any of the policemen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't remember if I said, but I have said that I have seen insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if it did not appear in your statement, that would again be a mistake of the person who took the statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: They haven't asked me. If they had asked me, I would have said they had camouflage uniforms and patches on their arms. But The Hague Tribunal did ask me what uniforms the police was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if they have asked you and that it wasn't recorded, sir, would you agree that it's the person who took the statement who failed to mention it in your statement? Is that what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness just said that they haven't asked me. So now I don't understand if they asked the following question --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps I'm confused by the last part of the answer of the witness. He said but The Hague did ask me what uniform the police was wearing. I understood the witness now to be saying that he was asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I think that there are two issues. One issue is the uniforms. The other are the patches so --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take it, sir, one step at a time. Did the Prosecution, the Office of the Prosecutor, when they first met you in the village of Ljuboten ask you about what uniforms the police was wearing?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you identified one policeman with a camouflage uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Not one policeman, several policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if your statement suggested that you have only identified one policeman with a camouflage uniform, you are saying that the person who took this statement failed to put that down in your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, your statement, sir, records you as saying that one policeman in camouflage uniform carrying an automatic weapon was guarding us. Then you talk about another policeman without any mention of his clothes. That's the only two policemen you are mentioning in your statement. So I'm asking you: You did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the only one mention of clothing of policemen --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- in the statement. The effect of the statement is clearly to indicate there were at different times and in different places a number of policemen. The subject of clothing is not mentioned. I think we understand exactly what you're saying, but the way you're putting it to the witness, it becomes quite confusing, and it's one thing what actually happened in the witness's evidence. It's another thing whether he has described that correctly when he was interviewed and yet a third thing, whether what he described was fully written down when he was interviewed, and I think they are being blurred, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, can you recall -- or are you suggesting that now you mentioned more than one police officer wearing a camouflage uniform in the corridor of the Skopje courtroom, sir, or did you only mention one at the time, or can't you recall?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I remember I said that there were several policemen in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if you have mentioned that there were several policemen in camouflage uniform at the time and that your statement only records one, that would be, again, a mistake of the person who took the statement, right?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, he didn't make a mistake. Why do you say he would have made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, just as a matter of clarification, if your statement was mentioning specifically only one policeman in camouflage uniform and you have now just told me that -- you mention that several policemen in camouflage uniform, your statement would inaccurately reflect what you told this person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you have also been asked about patches. Is that your evidence, sir that prior to yesterday, you had never been asked about what patches the police officers in the corridor were wearing. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just to be clear: Were you asked prior to yesterday or was it the first time yesterday that you were asked about patches worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I was asked even before, related to these patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you were asked, were you asked about those patches the first time when you met with the Office of the Prosecution in Ljuboten on 30 September 2004?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. We need to have a break now and we will resume at 11.00. The court officer will take you out in a moment. We adjourn now until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a person, a fellow villager, by the name Isni Ali?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've met with him in The Hague in the course of this week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you discuss with Mr. Ali the evidence which you are giving today, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you discuss the issue of the policemen present in the corridor of the court in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, if Mr. Ali were to say that the uniform worn by the police in the corridor of the courtroom were of a blue colour, you would say he's wrong, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Well, he can give his responses and I can give mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, do you know a person called Vebi Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: As a fellow villager.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And you also know, sir, that this person testified before the Tribunal recently, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you didn't meet him here in The Hague; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, no. I have met him, but I don't know whether it's him, actually, because I know him only by Vehbi, I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bajrami said this to the Prosecutor on the 8th of June, 2007: Vehbi Bajrami thinks that the policemen who beat the other detained people from Ljuboten at Skopje Court were court police and not the same policemen who were at Mirkovci police station. Do you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't know what he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But would you agree with his suggestion that the people who did the beating at the court were court police?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't know what he saw while he was at the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you, perhaps, sir, would you agree that the police whom you saw mistreating people at the court were court police, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You've indicated to my colleague and in your statement that you were mistreated prior to and at the time when you were in Skopje Court, is that correct, in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say that you bore the marks, the bruises of those beatings at the time?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: You mean bodily injuries?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Including on your face?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, and I have a scar on my face.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those bodily injuries, sir, they remained apparent for quite some time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes, during the time I was in prison for those four months. And later on they healed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification, sir, of the date. Is that correct that you were eventually released on the 14th of December of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, the reason why you were brought before the court in Skopje related to charges that you had committed an act of terrorism; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, weren't you charged and indicted for a crime of terrorism under Article 313 of the criminal code, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I was charged for that, but I never carried out terrorist acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P50. That would be ET-N002-0138-1. And the Macedonian version would be N002-0084-55.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this document says that it's a criminal charge. It is submitted against Farush Memedi, father Husein, mother Beguse, born on 27 March 1965 in Skopje, municipality of Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And if you look at the top left corner of that document, it says that the document comes from internal affairs unit, Cair, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is dated 14 August 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that it's being sent to the basic public prosecutor in Skopje? That's the next line, sir.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I never saw this document. I'm seeing it for the first time today. Maybe it is addressed to the organ you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in any case, that's what the document says; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the document says, but I didn't know of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go down to the bottom of that page, that first page, sir, it says that due to presence of founding suspicious -- suspicion, I'm sorry, that he committed a criminal act terrorism according to Article 313 of the criminal code of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask the registry to go to the third page after that document in English. And that would also be the third page in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I draw your attention to the first paragraph on that page 3. It is also the first paragraph in the Macedonian. It says that, "The reported persons prepared the obtained weapons and ammunition to be used in the morning hours on 12 August 2001. Proceeding around 8.00 to initiate a direct attack on the positions of the joint Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia, located in the area of the village Ljuboten, with the aim to destroy them and to endanger the constitutional order and security of the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that paragraph, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you go further down in that document, jumping over one paragraph, there's a paragraph starting: "In OVR Kisela Voda." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says that, "In OVR Kisela Voda official conversation was conducted with the aforementioned persons on which an Official Note was put together. We have enclosed this Official Note." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes to say that, "After the conducted conversation with the reported persons, paraffin gloves were taken with -- which were then submitted to expert processing of MOI of Republic of Macedonia, criminalistic technical department. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says, "The MOI of the Republic of Macedonia criminalistic technical department has informed us with expert report number 10.2.6-29838-1, dated 14 August 2001, that the result for the gun powder particles were positive for the reported persons. We have enclosed the expert report with this charge." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in the last paragraph, sir, the person who wrote that document says the following: "The elements of a committed criminal terrorism envisaged and punishable in accordance with Article 313 of the criminal code of the Republic of Macedonia are evident from the aforementioned -- and the submitted facts. We therefore propose that you submit a request for conducting an investigation against the reported persons in order to prove the criminal act and the criminal responsibility of the reported persons." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is signed by the head of the OVR Cair, Mr. Lube Krstevski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd wish to tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, my fault. I think it has been admitted already as part of the P50. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, is that correct that all of the other persons mentioned on that document were also from the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And all of these persons had tested positive to nitrate particles; is that correct? Or are you not able to say?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No. I'm speaking of myself. I don't know for the others, but personally, as far as I'm concerned, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You can blame the counsel for the question, not yourself. Is that correct or is that --

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you have answered my question, sir, and I think you made it clear that you -- am I correct to understand that you do not know of the results of the paraffin glove tests in relation to the other people mentioned on that document? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: This is not very clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll move on, sir. Are you aware of the fact that a number of villagers who had been brought in to the police were immediately released from the police station, or soon thereafter?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: We were released the following day, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be the Monday, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't remember the day, but I know that a number of fellow villagers were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, they were released because their paraffin test was negative? Is that something which is within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown another document, which is P51, page 3 in the English, and it is P51 N001-9987-07.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may draw your attention to the first paragraph of that document at the top, it say: "The investigating judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, Ognen Stavrev, deciding upon the request for implementation of the investigation submitted by basic public prosecution Skopje with a proposal to determine measure, detention under KO number 2801-01 dated 4 -- 14 August 2001 against accused Memedi Farush, and then it goes on to list a number of other people. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go further down you can see that the nature of that document is a decision of enforcement of investigation against, and the first name to appear is yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask you to turn or the registry to turn to the second page of the English and that would also be the second page of the Macedonian. Sir, I'll ask you to look at the second paragraph on that page, once it appears on your screen. It says the following: "These activities derived a well-founded suspicion that accused Memedi Farush and a number of others, each of them committed by one criminal act of terrorism pursuant to Article 313 from KZ," KZ standing for criminal code [Realtime transcript read in error: "court"]. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then underneath you can see that the person who prepared that document presents what is being translated as an argument. Can you see that? It's a subheading sir, under the Roman II numbering.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think my French English has betrayed me, Your Honour. Have said -- or I should have said "criminal code" and it has been recorded as "criminal court" at transcript page 46, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you French English manages much better than my Australian English when it comes to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, if I may ask to you look at that third page of that document now. You'll see that the document come from Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, KI, and it is dated 14 August 2001 again. And it is signed by investigating judge Ognen Stavrev. Can you see that? Sorry, sir, you haven't yet received the documents. I will ask you my question again. Can you see a signature, sir, on that page?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
