utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It says investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Above that line there is a note or a phrase saying Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, KI number 439-01 and it is dated 14 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you look at the last paragraph of that decision, there is something which has been translated as "on advice," and it said, "Period of three days is allowed to lodge a complaint against the decision of enforcement of an investigation when the decision has been received and it is allowed a period of 24 hours to lodge a complaint against the decision for detention and it is submitted -- and it is to be submitted through the investigative judge to the criminal counsel of this court." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document. It's again admitted already, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember receiving that document at all?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown -- I'd like the witness to be shown another document, which is Exhibit P51. It's at page 28 in the English version. And in the Macedonian version it is P51, page N001-9987-25.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you look first perhaps at the right-hand corner there is a number which is the same number as I read out to you earlier, which is 439-01. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And underneath, there is a date, which says 15 August 2001, and underneath --

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- your name, Farush Memedi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the left side it says village of Ljuboten, Ognen Stavrev. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page of the document, it says that the interview started at 3.05. Then there's an advice about the use of your own language. And I would like you to turn to the next paragraph where it starts: "He was informed that basic public prosecution." Can you see that? That's the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says that he was informed that basic public prosecution Skopje under KO number 2801 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not seem to have the right English version. I apologise, Mr. Memedi. The English should be Exhibit P51, page 28 and there's an ERN -- yes. I'm grateful to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, sir. Can I ask you once against to turn to the second paragraph. It says that, "He was informed that basic public prosecution Skopje under KO number 2801-01 dated 14 August 2001 submitted a request on enforcement of investigation within the proposal to pose detention because of the well-based suspicion the accused committed a criminal act of terrorism, pursuant to Article 313 from KZ, criminal code," and it is stated that you understood it. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then the next paragraph, it says that, "Pursuant to Article 3, paragraph 2, and Article 63, paragraphs 1 and 2 from the ZKP, the accused was advised that a defence attorney appointed by him can be present at his interrogation. Hence, he stated that he would like Tahir Fidovski, an attorney from Skopje, appointed to him as a defence attorney by ex officio and who was present at today's hearing to act as a defence attorney on his behalf." Sir, before I go any further with this document, do you recall having that meeting with Mr. -- with Judge Stavrev?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: There was a lawyer there, but I don't know him. I don't know whether he was a lawyer or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you don't remember the name of that person, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Correct. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if we look at the next paragraph, sir, it says -- and that's the last line. Well, I mean first the first line. You were informed that you had the right not to respond to any questions. And the last sentence says, "Therefore, the accused stated he will use the entitled right and he will remain silent." And that's correct, sir, that's what you already told me earlier today. You decided to remain silent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: It wasn't possible for me to speak and that's why I said that. I was very much beaten, maltreated. I was not in a position to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it concludes, "I do not have anything else to stay. These minutes been read out loud to me and I accept it as my own and I put my signature onto it," and you went on to sign it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: I don't remember signing it but it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will not move to have it admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, while you were in this meeting with Mr. Stavrev, you did not raise any complaint with him of mistreatment or beatings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: He could see us by himself. He could see us that we are beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you didn't tell him anything, you didn't raise any complaint to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Didn't he have eyes to see?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I can't ask you a question about what Mr. Stavrev did or saw. I'm asking you did you make any complaint to Mr. Judge Stavrev about what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: For this reason, we -- we didn't have the opportunity to speak-- the possibility to speak in the court because I was very beaten up and I couldn't speak. This is the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, but my question is slightly different. Is that correct that did you not raise any complaint with Judge Stavrev about what had happened to you in the days and hours prior to this interview? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: How could I complain? I don't understand that question, how to complain. Tell the police to complain? I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My question is as follows, sir: You did not tell Mr. Stavrev, Judge Stavrev, that you had been beaten at Kisela Voda police station, for instance?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, I didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You didn't tell him either that you had been beaten prior to that time at another police station?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the lawyer who was present with you on that day, he didn't make any complaint or did not make any remark in relation to those -- to the judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is under the same large Exhibit P50 and in the English it is under the ERN ET-N002-0128-01. And the Macedonian version of that document is under N002-0084-45.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the top of the document, it says that it's the public prosecutor's office. Then there is a number, 2801-2, 2001. Skopje, 7 September, 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the next line suggest that it is being sent to the Lower Court Skopje II, Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the title of that document is "indictment." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to list a number of individuals who have been indicted, Mr. Ali Riza under number one. Qamuran Rexhepi under number 2. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the third page of that document in the English, and that would be page number 3, although it is the fourth page of Macedonian with an ERN 0084-48.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. It's the third -- the second page in the English and it would be the third page in the Macedonian. I apologise to the registry. The ERN for the Macedonian is 0084-47.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you have number 9 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that refers to you, Farush Memedi, father Husein, mother Beguse and born on 27 of March 1965. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can go to the fourth page of the English version, it is ET-N002-012804. And it is also page 4 of the Macedonian version. Sorry. That would be the next page in both languages. Your Honour, there seems to be a difference between the documents that I have in front of me and the documents that appears on the screen. The English version should be ET N002-0128-04, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, there seems to be a difference between the documents that I have in front of me and the documents that appears on the screen. The English version should be ET N002-0128-04 in the English. Your Honour, there seems to be a problem with the pagination, but I think we can go directly to the last page of the document. That will save everyone's time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, if we go to the last paragraph but one, it starts with the words "this defence of the accused." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a paragraph, the last paragraph and that's the one I want you to focus on. It says: "In consideration of the above, I find that the actions of the accused Ali Riza," and then there's a number name. Can you see your name appearing further down the list? It's the last paragraph, sir.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the deputy prosecutor moves on to say, "I move that they be found guilty and that in determining the type and length of the sentence, the Court should weigh both the mitigating and aggravating circumstances." Can you see that? And just -- well, just above perhaps before you respond to my question it relates to a crime which is said to contain the elements qualifying the crime of service in an enemy army from Article 322, paragraph 1 of the criminal code. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it charges -- it goes on to charge you with participating in an armed attack as combatants against the Republic of Macedonia. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it moves on to suggest that you should be found guilty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: Well, this is not true. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you like a break, sir? Are you ...

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI
utterances.text: If possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying you need just a short break or would you like a longer break? I'm not sure what the position is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A short break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn, I think, for a quarter of an hour, Mr. Mettraux, and resume at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 11.45 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We delayed our return as we heard the witness was still not well. Time having now stretched even further, I think it's time to consider again where we should proceed with the rest of today. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been informed by the Victims and Witness Unit that the witness who was testifying before the break is not able to continue today and therefore I would propose that the Prosecution commence with witness M-056, who is prepared now to testify, seems to be in very good health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, let us hope. We are getting a growing list of people who are not able to see through the -- the whole course. Very well. Thank you for being able to arrange that. And we proceed with the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an application to make before the witness comes, and I would like to ask if we could please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, briefly into private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So the Prosecution will call now Witness M-056, Your Honour. I think it will take a minute or two for the witness to arrive in the courtroom. While we're waiting, may I have Your Honour's permission to make a brief and perhaps a rather strange application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, the application that the Prosecution needs to make is one I have never made before, at least not in this Tribunal. It is it to exclude some Prosecution evidence that has been admitted. And I will explain the rather unique circumstances that arose. I believe yesterday, with the last Prosecution witness who became ill, counsel for the Prosecution attempted to admit into evidence under Rule 92 bis an addendum that had been produced during proofing, which was an addendum which had not been certified according to the Rule, and counsel rightfully objected and the Trial Chamber rightfully ruled that there was no legal basis to admit that addendum. However, it's the Prosecution's understanding that earlier this week, a similar addendum was tendered under Rule 92 bis and the Trial Chamber admitted it, and I believe it is due to a misunderstanding between Prosecution counsel at that moment and the Trial Chamber. And I would -- I'm referring to what was admitted as Exhibit P247.2. It was an -- it was submitted as an addendum to the witness statement of Vebi Bajrami. Prosecution believes that it was actually -- there was actually no proper legal basis for that addendum to be admitted, and so the Prosecution would ask the Trial Chamber that it remove that addendum from the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were there consequences in the course of questioning by either Prosecution or Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm looking at the question whether it might be necessary if this motion were granted to recall the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the parties would have to carefully look at the transcript before I could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon, and thank you indeed for the promptness and the honesty with which the matter is brought before us. The document was admitted, I believe, without objection, from memory. We would like you and, if necessary, after discussion with Defence counsel to look at the consequences of the motion on the effective questioning that followed of the witness, so that we don't want to create the position where it is necessary to recall the witness because this foundation for the way it was dealt with is removed after he is gone. So could we simply delay dealing with your motion, ask you to look at the implications, as we've indicated, and we will hear from you whenever it is next convenient, in your judgment, to bring the matter up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Perhaps -- well -- Your Honour, would the Trial Chamber permit me to approach the Bench and provide you with packages of exhibits that we intend to show the next witness? The usher is not in the room right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the Chamber's legal officer or the registry officer approach you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is on the card shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The microphone isn't turned on. I apologise Your Honours. It was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. So that you are aware, sir, you will be informed that your evidence is being given with protective measures. Both your voice and your face will be distorted, so that it ought not to be possible to identify you outside those that are in this courtroom, and we will be referring to you by the pseudonym of Witness 56. So that your name won't be used in the courtroom. And that having been said, I believe Mr. Saxon has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before I start my questions if I could ask for the assistance the usher to put this piece of paper, it has ERN number N006-4863, if that could be placed in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Witness, do you see the piece of paper in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And without stating your name, is that your correct name that's written on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is the other information written on that piece of paper correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: They are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Witness, today I will be referring to you as M-056 or 56. I will not address you by your true name. If there are situations where I need to ask you questions which might identify you, then I will ask to move into what we call private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher's assistance, please, to show that piece of paper to Defence counsel. And, Your Honours, if Defence counsel have no objection, then I would move that this document be admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, before I forget.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P270, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I forget, Your Honours, there is a mistake in the index in the binder of documents that has been provided to you. I'd simply like to point it out to you so that there is no confusion created. It's on page 2 of the index at what is marked as item 21, and the description of item 21 begins: "Two video recordings," and then it gives a date and the date listed there is 3 May 2005. That is incorrect, Your Honour. The date should be written 7 May 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that maybe there is a mistake because the learned colleague refers to a document he was -- he was showing this document is to Goran Georgievski, the son of Bojko, not Georgievski Bojko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that clarification. I obviously did not understand the structure of the English translation. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are in public session, are we? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, I'd like you to turn your mind, please, to the month of May in 2001. In the middle of May 2001 was the -- were the Tigers units operating in the area of a village called Vaksince?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: In -- in the vicinity of the village of Vaksince. Not in the village of Vaksince.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I stand corrected; I appreciate that. If we could now please show the witness the map of Macedonia which is on page 2 of the court binder, please. This would be tab 5 of the binder. No, that's not correct. It would be tab 3, yes, you were right. Witness M-056, just briefly, please, if I can turn your attention to the northern part of the country of Macedonia on this map. Can you indicate, tell us where the village of Vaksince is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: It's near the village of Lojane, which is on the very Macedonian-Albanian border and next to the Tabanovce village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that Vaksince is located to the north, a bit to the north-west of the town of Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, why were the Tiger units deployed near Vaksince in May of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: To arrest terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what was going on in the Vaksince area in May of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: The entire territory was full of terrorists that were well established with heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was there fighting ongoing between the groups you referred to as the terrorists and the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, fortified instead of established.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show the Chamber and the witness and the parties some video material. And, Your Honours, if I turn to tab 4, you will see the transcript of some video clips. These are videos from the Prosecution's 65 ter exhibit number 975. It's video footage that was shot by the Macedonian television in May of 2001. And it comes from the archive of Macedonian Radio and Television. And initially I would like to show the witness a clip that runs from 0905 to 1255. And we may pause a couple of times so that I can ask questions to the witness about what we're seeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, if you're able to help us, Witness, these gentlemen in the back of that truck, would they be members of the Macedonian army, the police or some other institution, if you can tell?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's at 23:5 on the counter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that precision, Your Honour. I will do that in the future.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes, these are members of the regular forces of the Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are members of the regular forces of the Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we pause right there, at 1:04:7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we pause there, please. Well, the picture is bit blurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you able in what you have seen so far to identify the gentleman who's in the grey jacket, and this is the 01197. Do you recognise that gentleman, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: That is the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that Ljube Boskoski at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness M-056, why Mr. Boskoski came to the area around Vaksince at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek to tender that last clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P272, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue with the next clip, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, can you tell us what we're seeing here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: We see an army combat helicopter Mi-24.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why were such helicopters used around the area of Vaksince at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Because we could not act in a different way. The terrorist forces were acting against with us heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel turn the microphone on. We are not able to hear. Could the counsel repeat. The interpreters were not able to hear her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, because the microphone was turned away from you, the interpreters couldn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The Prosecutor did not establish the grounds for the last question that he asked, because the witness, before that, did not say anything whether helicopters were used on the territory of Vaksince, and I think it would be necessary that the previous question is whether there was helicopters there at all, and then to suggest to the witness the question that was just asked by my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, when you were deployed at the area around Vaksince, did you observe helicopters being used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Not around Vaksince, but around Slupcane.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is Slupcane near Vaksince?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: It's next to Vaksince. It is a little bit bigger than Vaksince.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And how were such helicopters used at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: They were used to observe, to enter -- and to destroy potential attackers that were attacking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, can you explain to us what that helicopter is doing, why we see those bright lights coming off of it? This is at 00:34:8.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: I did not see at this recording what the helicopter is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, do you know why -- during the crisis time, do you know why such helicopters shot off these types of flares or lights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: These flares are fired to defend the helicopter from stingers or rocket launchers from the ground that those were launchers that the NLA members had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Keep going, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you look at now -- we're 58:9 and we see a house there. That appears to be - if I can use the vernacular - going up literally in smoke, While you were deployed in this area in May of 2001, did the fighting take place close to or even in the villages themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Most frequently in the vicinity of the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see Mr. Boskoski standing there. This is at 02.13.0. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There's a man standing behind Mr. Boskoski in what appears to be a black jacket on what is our left, and he has what appears to be a shaven head. Do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When the Tiger units were deployed around the area of Vaksince, did they participate in operations with members of the Macedonian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes we had coordinated actions together with the army of the Republic of Macedonia members.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in those -- when the Tiger units were participating in coordinated actions, how many -- with the army, how many chains of command did you respond to at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: During the war, our unit was placed under the command of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you also respond to the chain of command of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why was the situation in the area around Vaksince so difficult for the security forces of Macedonia in May of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Because first there was a big number of them. I referred to the terrorists. Then they had very well established defence. They had the advantage of the configuration. Not just configuration, they had many trenches and lots of equipment. It is impossible to get there quickly or easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can just move a few more seconds along this video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think you just heard Mr. Boskoski speak about moving forward step by step and until we return the constitutional order to Macedonia. Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: By May of 2001, what had happened to the constitutional order of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: The security was endangered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why was it in danger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Because we were attacked by larger or smaller, depending on the location of that deployment, terrorist groups of NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could just finish this clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this last clip, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P273, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next clip begins at 53:20 of this video and will go to about 54:55. If we could start it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, when you and your units were deployed in the area around Vaksince in May of 2001, did you observe numbers of persons who were displaced by the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them going out of the Albanian villages. It was the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, a moment ago you explained that you saw numbers of persons in May of 2001 who had been displaced by the fighting and that -- that these were the civilian population who had left the Albanian villages. What instructions did you give to the members of your units in terms of how to treat these civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: My unit had no contact with these civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you give any instructions to the members of your unit as to how they should treat civilians if they encountered them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: We did not issue additional instructions because that has been agreed previously, how to act with civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what was -- to use your term, what was the agreement that had been agreed on previously in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: The civilians are always treated in a proper manner with due respect to their rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And civilians would not be beaten, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056
utterances.text: Yes, civilians should not be beaten unless they show resistance, unless they are armed, and unless it is found that there is something else behind that civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue with this video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender that last video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P274, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move into private session again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
